transmitter_eye_reference_per_phy: MDI compliance eyes are specified per PMD clause: Figure 14-9 for 10BASE-T, Figure 25-? for 100BASE-TX, Figures 40-19..40-28 for 1000BASE-T. RJ-45 MDI return loss / NEXT specifications are also per PMD clause.
general_timing_rule: All MII / GMII signals are synchronous to TX_CLK (TX path) or RX_CLK (RX path); MDC is asynchronous. Bit times scale linearly with line rate (100 ns at 10 Mb/s, 10 ns at 100 Mb/s, 1 ns at 1 Gb/s); inter-frame gap = 96 BT and slot time = 512 BT (10/100 Mb/s) or 4096 BT (1 Gb/s) are both expressed in bit times so the same MAC FSM scales across the speed range.

frame_timing_at_100mbps.comment: Frame transmission at 100 Mb/s carries one wire-bit every 10 ns.

ethercat_datagram_timing.comment: Throughput: 1 datagram with N data bytes = (12+N)*80 ns on wire at 100 Mb/s.

esc_forwarding_latency_ns.comment: ESC forwards the in-flight frame in cut-through mode; per-hop delay is dominated by the on-the-fly engine pipeline depth, NOT by store-and-forward.

distributed_clocks_timing.comment: DC field engineering target: <100 ns network-wide jitter. Verified by network analyzer comparing SYNC0 rising edges across hops.

cyclic_exchange_timing.comment: Cycle time is bounded below by ((frame transmission time) + Σ ESC forwarding delays + cable propagation + MainDevice software jitter). For 100 SubDevices on 100 Mb/s with 16 B I/O each, the wire time is ~140 µs.

pdi_timing.comment: PDI is the application-side bus to local µC; choice is configured in 0x0140 PDI Control.
